items.title: CLAIR OBSCUR: EXPEDITION 33 Director Calls KINGDOM HEARTS 2 "One of the Best Action RPGs Ever Created," Says He's Been Chasing Its Gameplay Ever Since
items.content:
If you've spent any time with Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , you've probably noticed that it proudly celebrates the games that helped shape it. From its love of classic Final Fantasy to the stylish action that feels right at home alongside Devil May Cry , its inspirations aren't exactly hidden.

Now, the game's creative director, Guillaume Broche , has opened up about another major influence, and it's one that plenty of RPG fans will happily agree with.

During an appearance on Konbini's Jeux Video Club series, Broche praised Kingdom Hearts 2 as one of the greatest action RPGs ever made, explaining that its combat has been the gold standard for him ever since.

Broche revealed that Kingdom Hearts 2 sits comfortably among his favorite games ever made, saying it's one of his "top five games of all time." He also gave credit to Square Enix for creating something truly special.

He said: "You have to admit that Square Enix has managed to create something truly exceptional."

While the Kingdom Hearts series has always been known for blending Disney worlds with fast-paced action, it's the combat in the second game that Broche believes stands above the rest. The fluid mechanics, flashy abilities, and rewarding progression clearly left a lasting impression on him.

As he explained: "There's really something about that gameplay that I've been looking for ever since Kingdom Hearts 2."

He also pointed to the game's deep endgame systems, especially the increasingly satisfying combat options players unlock later in the adventure, saying: "You could spend 150 hours in the late game."

Broche also shared his thoughts on the more recent entry in the series, saying: "Kingdom Hearts 3 isn't bad, but it didn't manage to recapture everything it did in terms of gameplay, which was exceptional."

It's an opinion that many longtime Kingdom Hearts fans have debated over the years. While Kingdom Hearts 3 delivered spectacular visuals and massive set pieces, plenty of players have argued that Kingdom Hearts 2 still offers the tighter and more rewarding combat system.

Looking at Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , it's easy to see how those influences found their way into the finished game. The title embraces classic RPG ideas inspired by Final Fantasy, while Verso's combat style clearly channels Devil May Cry .

Broche has even shared Devil May Cry challenge runs online before developing Clair Obscur, and fans have been quick to point out similarities between Verso's ranking system, moveset, and Vergil's iconic combat style.

With that mix of action and RPG mechanics at the heart of Clair Obscur , it makes perfect sense that Kingdom Hearts 2 would also be one of the games that helped shape Broche's creative vision.

Great games tend to leave a lasting mark on the developers who grow up playing them, and in this case, one of gaming's most beloved action RPGs helped inspire one of 2025's biggest breakout hits.

items.title: Sony’s Decision To End Physical Discs Is ‘Super Sad’ ,Says Expedition 33 Director
items.summary: Expedition 33's directors call Sony's move away from physical discs “super sad,” citing ownership, preservation, and the value of discs.
items.content:
Expedition 33's directors call Sony's move away from physical discs “super sad,” citing ownership, preservation, and the value of boxed editions.

Sony’s move away from physical game discs has disappointed the developers behind Game of the Year 2025, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 .

Speaking about the future of boxed games, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 creative director Guillaume Broche and lead programmer Tom Guillermin expressed disappointment over Sony’s decision to stop producing physical discs.

In an interview with Automaton , the developers called the decision “super sad” and emphasized that physical ownership is something they value as players, not merely as game creators.

Personally, I find it super sad because I really like video game stores. And even if nowadays, I play mainly on PC myself, we have a lot of people on the team who play on PS5 and love to collect physical discs. I think it’s part of the beauty of art too – that it’s something tangible that you can touch. I completely appreciate that people want to have their rows of DVDs and games and just feel that they own them. So I think it’s a shame. I mean, business-wise, I can understand why it may make sense, but I think in terms of the artistry of video games, it’s a sad decision. – Guillaume Broche

A physical edition is more than another product SKU for collectors; it provides a tangible copy that can be displayed, shared, resold, and preserved without depending entirely on a digital storefront.

Sandfall Interactive still pushed for a physical version of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , even though producing one came with drawbacks. Sandfall’s CTO Tom Guillermin said there is more loss per unit in a physical copy, but they still pushed for people who enjoyed physical releases.

A physical release adds more constraints because you have to account for the production time of the physical items, and you also earn less money per copy.

So even though it made things harder and meant less money per unit, it was important for us to provide players who want to have the physical game in their hands with an option. Because that’s what we value as players too. – Tom Guillermin

Physical editions require manufacturing, distribution, inventory planning, and coordination between a developer and its publishing partners. Those complications are especially relevant for a smaller studio that cannot rely on the enormous production runs available to the industry’s biggest publishers.

It was the harder route, but they still took it because to them physical was special.

But for us, physical was something special. We also felt that the game could be special to players, and that they would want to, as Guillaume said, hold it in their hands. – Tom Guillermin

The team reportedly purchased boxed copies of its own RPG, which says plenty about how personally it viewed the release.

To add to that, there were two very strong moments when the game released. After launch, we went to a video game store to buy our own game (laughs). – Guillaume Broche

items.title: The Switch 2 is already starting to show its seams
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Giovanni Colantonio Published Aug 1, 2026, 9:00 AM EDT Switchboard Getting big games running on Nintendo's console is no easy task

Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen is officially getting a hard mode A free new Batman game just quietly dropped on Amazon Deadpool goes Super Saiyan in final Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls trailer The Switch 2 is already starting to show its seams Image: Sandfall interactive/Kepler Interactive Sign in to your Polygon.com account Switchboard is Polygon's weekly newsletter for all things Nintendo, sent on Thursdays and published on the site on Saturdays. You can subscribe here .

Just one year into the Switch 2’s lifespan, Nintendo’s console feels like a technical miracle. It’s downright shocking that it can run modern games like Resident Evil Requiem and Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth with minimal compromises, or that new games like Onimusha: Way of the Sword will launch on it at the same time as on PS5 and Xbox Series X. For Nintendo fans who spent decades pining for third-party games that never came to underpowered machines like the Wii, it feels like the Switch 2 can do it all. Except it can’t.

We got a reality check this week courtesy of Sandfall Interactive, the developer of last year’s Game of the Year winning Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . In a new interview with Automaton Media , Sandfall co-founder Tom Guillermin explained that the team wants to bring its hit RPG to Switch 2, but said that it would be a “big technical challenge” to pull off.

The problem? Unreal Engine 5. Clair Obscur heavily relied on the engine’s features to make its game, especially taking advantage of Blueprints (a scripting tool that lets developers plug nodes together to craft gameplay systems). The team said that many of those features simply don’t work on Switch 2 at present. “They’re introducing features like Lumen Lite now, which is easier to run than the standard Lumen,” lead character and concept artist Alan Reynaud explained, “but these things take time to roll out, so we’ll have to consider the updates coming from Unreal Engine to determine what to do.” With some Switch 2 ports, developers are simply at the mercy of Epic for now.

This isn’t the first example of a developer struggling to get its game working on Switch 2. Last year, 2K Games indefinitely delayed the Switch 2 release of Borderlands 4 for “additional development and polish time.” Closing in on one year later, we haven’t heard a peep about it since. (Though Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick told Game File that the project hadn't been cancelled earlier this year.)

Image: FromSoftware/Bandai Namco Then there’s the long-running saga of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition . First announced during the Switch 2’s full reveal Direct with a 2025 release window, the port faced a year-long delay after hands-on impressions out of last year’s Gamescom raised some serious red flags. Finally set to release on Aug. 28, Elden Ring will now land as a crucial stress test for Switch 2. FromSoftware’s ability to get the open-world game — one that was released on PS4 and Xbox One — running well on the hardware will tell us a lot about how flexible Nintendo’s dream machine is. (The good news is that it seems to be in much better shape than it was last year.)

The reality is that the Switch 2 still has its limits, even though companies like Capcom and Square Enix have seemingly cracked the console’s code. It takes hard work to get Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth running on the hardware, and that’s a challenge for smaller teams like Sandfall Interactive who may not have the resources to invest in time-consuming ports. We’re still far off from a reality where every third-party game will get a Switch 2 version, and that will only become apparent if a new console generation begins midway through the Switch 2’s lifespan.

Never forget that The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild felt like a miracle when fans first played it on the go in 2017. Eight years later, Switch owners were begging for an upgrade. That’s the nature of hardware, and the Switch 2 will not be immune to that cycle in the long run.

The formerly VR-exclusive Moss series made its way to consoles this month, and it feels right at home on Switch. The pair of games featured in Moss: The Forgotten Relic are both delightful, kind-hearted adventures starring an adorable mouse. (The pint-sized hero melted Austin Manchester’s heart, as you can read in his review .) It doesn’t get much more Nintendo than that.

A classic arcade series makes its return this week with Truxton Extreme , so it’s a good weekend to pay some respects to Truxton creator Toplan, the master of the shoot-’em-up genre. The best way to do that is by jumping into one of its most iconic games, Mega Drive classic Zero Wing . Yes, it’s the game that gave us “All your base are belong to us,” but it’s also a tense sci-fi shump with a killer soundtrack to boot.

It feels like summer just began, but we’ve already reached August. Don’t let the last few weeks of heat slip away; toss on the Wave Race 64 soundtrack today. It’s full of sunny beachside anthems, including this radical prog rock jam that feels like it was plucked right out of an 80s movie. (There's a playlist of all of Switchboard's music picks here .)

Xenoblade Chronicles 2 — Nintendo Switch 2 Edition

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 took inspiration from Attack on Titan and Bleach's instantly recognizable characters: "It's an absolute masterpiece for me"
items.summary: "When you see any character from Attack on Titan, you instantly know they
items.content:
"When you see any character from Attack on Titan, you instantly know they're an Attack on Titan character," director Guillaume Broche says

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Kepler Interactive) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Much has been said about how Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 pulled heavily from classic JRPGs - Final Fantasy, Persona, Lost Odyssey, etc - but the hit game also drew lots of inspiration from some of the best anime shows around, including Attack on Titan and Bleach.

Speaking to Automaton about the game's influences, Sandfall Interactive CEO Guillaume Broche says "one of the anime that inspired me for Expedition 33's story was Attack on Titan." Both have pretty existential themes and a cast of characters who are almost constantly face-to-face with a life-ending threat that seems inevitable.

"I really like the idea of a group of heroes fighting together, and I especially love the uniform," Broche explains. "When you see any character from Attack on Titan, you instantly know they're an Attack on Titan character because of the uniform. That's something I really wanted to bring over into Expedition 33, making the game recognizable just from its uniforms."

Broche then mentions he's midway through a series rewatch, "and really, it's an absolute masterpiece for me." Hear, hear.

Attack on Titan's instantly recognizable cast and sleek uniforms weren't the only anime-flavored well the team at Sandfall drew from. Lead character and concept artist, Alan Reynaud, shouts out Bleach as another important touchstone for the studio: "I have to mention Bleach because the character designs in the series are spectacular. One of the things we took from it was designs that are super simple yet incredibly memorable. We wanted to have something like that, with a 'rule of cool' approach. I'd say that was a big inspiration for the character creation."

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 developer would love to bring game to Switch 2, but ‘it’s too early for us to announce anything’
items.summary: In a new interview with Automaton about the inspiration behind its hit turn-based RPG, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 developer Sandfall Interactive was asked
items.content:
In a new interview with Automaton about the inspiration behind its hit turn-based RPG, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 developer Sandfall Interactive was asked about the potential for the game to hit Switch 2 in the future. Answering questions were Guillaume Broche, the game’s director, Tom Guillermin, CTO and co-founder of Sandfall, Alan Reynaud, lead character artist, and Alexandre Breton, lead technical artist at Sandfall. The official company stance? “It’s too early for us to announce anything.”

The majority of the interview focuses on how Sandfall believes limitations are what bring out the best aspects of game design. Naturally, this segued into a discussion about the Switch 2, which has more limited hardware specifications compared against the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X. Answering the question about a Switch 2 port directly, Broche commented, “We are interested in looking for a way to do it, but it’s too early for us to announce anything at this point.”

Elaborating further, Guillermin added, “It’s a big technical challenge because we tried to do something beautiful with the game, but of course, the Switch 2 is not as powerful as the PlayStation or the Xbox Series X. So, it’s an important thing for us to consider, especially given the size of our studio.” Broche mentions that “A lot of features [of Unreal Engine 5] don’t work on Switch 2.”

If you’ve been following the development of Unreal Engine 5, you’ll know that Epic Games has introduced some new features which are aimed specifically at Switch 2 development. As Reynaud brings up, “They’re [Epic Games] introducing features like Lumen Lite now, which is easier to run than the standard Lumen, but these things take time to roll out, so we’ll have to consider the updates coming from Unreal Engine to determine what to do.” Backporting that into Clair Obscur would be a bigger task than simply flicking a switch and being set.

All things considered, it doesn’t seem like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 will be hitting the Switch 2 anytime soon. While Sandfall probably doesn’t want to overlook the opportunity to bring its game to a wider audience, it might not be technologically feasible given how integral UE5 features were to the game’s look and design.

Peter has been a freelance gaming and film critic for over seven years. His passion for Nintendo is only matched by the size of his collection.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 devs are working on a Nintendo Switch 2 version, but note the "big technical challenge" of getting it up and running
items.summary: Sandfall Interactive knows there is demand for a Switch 2 version of the breakout RPG, and the studio is working on it.
items.content:
Image credit: Eurogamer News by Dom Peppiatt Deputy Editorial Director Published on July 29, 2026, 12:01 p.m. 40 comments Follow Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Do you want to play Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on Switch 2 ? Since the launch of Nintendo's console, fans have been clamouring for the breakout RPG to come to the platform - and we've seen hints from the studio that a port is something it would be willing to explore in the future .

But it probably won't be as straightforward as simply porting the game across to Nintendo's platform, and now - in a new interview with Automaton - Sandfall Interactive has outlined the realities of getting a version of the game running on Switch 2.

"It's a big technical challenge because we tried to do something beautiful with the game, but of course, the Switch 2 is not as powerful as the PlayStation or the Xbox Series X," notes Tom Guillermin, chief technical officer and lead programmer at Sandfall Interactive. "So, it's an important thing for us to consider, especially given the size of our studio." Guillermin goes on to note that a lot of features on Unreal Engine 5 - the tech the game is built on - "don't work on Switch 2".

"[Epic is] introducing features like Lumen Lite now, which is easier to run than the standard Lumen, but these things take time to roll out, so we'll have to consider the updates coming from Unreal Engine to determine what to do," adds lead character artist, Alan Reynaud.

So, when can we expect the game on Switch 2? There's no set time, says Sandfall Interactive CEO and creative director Guillaume Broche. "We are interested in looking for a way to do it, but it's too early for us to announce anything at this point."

Consider our expectations measured, then. It's fair enough, really, that the team is taking its time with something as complex as a Switch 2 port: Clair Obscur was created by a studio of around 30 people (with extra outsourced support). It sold a million copies in three days . In terms of what comes next, Broche himself has said that he doesn't really care what people think of its next game - a refreshing tonic to an industry increasingly chasing trends and relying on remakes and sequels in order to ensure returns on investment.

items.title: Unreal Engine 5 Made Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Possible, Yet It Makes A Nintendo Switch 2 Port A Big Challenge
items.summary: Sandfall Interactive reveals how Unreal Engine 5 made Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 possible, but also how it makes a Switch 2 port challenging
items.content:
Since its launch in 2022, Unreal Engine 5 has been one of the most controversial game engines from Epic Games , mostly due to how demanding it is on PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series X , and PC , as well as the performance issues it brings. Although the engine has been significantly improved since , public perception hasn't changed much, with many gamers considering it one of the worst things to happen to modern gaming. However, many developers don't share this sentiment, as Sandfall Interactive , the studio behind the 2025 Game of the Year Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , couldn't have made the game without it.

"For starters, Unreal Engine has all the tools you need to make a game that looks big, even if you’re not a big team," Sandfall Interactive CEO and Creative Director Guillaume Broche said to Automaton . "And we were very lucky with the release timing of some of Unreal’s newer tools. Unreal Engine 5 itself came at the right time in production, then MetaHuman came at the right time, and so did Nanite and Lumen – everything came at the right time. So we were very lucky with that."

The best thing about Unreal Engine 5 is that it gives developers all the tools they need to make something great, Broche continued, while heaping praise on Blueprints , the visual scripting system that will eventually be deprecated in Unreal Engine 6 , once the new Verse/Scene Graph framework matures. "Blueprints, especially, are very important. Blueprints are like a visual scripting method that allows pretty much anybody in the team to write code thanks to how easy it is. It’s like chaining blocks together. In our studio, we have four programmers, but every game designer and every technical artist uses Blueprints to make game logic or environment logic, and that’s crucial for us to be able to ship this kind of game and this kind of quality."

Technical Artist Alexandre Breton also had only praise for Unreal Engine 5's Blueprints . "Blueprints are part of an ecosystem. It’s visual scripting, so it’s very ludic and you can learn it very easily. It’s part of an ecosystem because a lot of people are using it and sharing content, so you can also find resources like tutorials everywhere. You can also find Blueprint Packs and learn from them. People give them away for free or sell them, and it’s never too expensive. Overall, it’s a system that’s very cool to use."

Although several games powered by Unreal Engine 5 have made their way onto the Nintendo Switch 2 , Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has yet to do so. The team is interested in a port, but there are technical challenges that are even more daunting for a small studio like Sandfall Interactive .

"It’s a big technical challenge because we tried to do something beautiful with the game, but of course, the Switch 2 is not as powerful as the PlayStation or the Xbox Series X. So, it’s an important thing for us to consider, especially given the size of our studio," said studio Co-founder and CTO Tom Guillermin .

While some Unreal Engine 5 features don't work on Nintendo Switch 2 , which we have known for a while, Lumen Lite could make the port slightly less challenging. "They’re introducing features like Lumen Lite now, which is easier to run than the standard Lumen, but these things take time to roll out, so we’ll have to consider the updates coming from Unreal Engine to determine what to do," said Lead Character and Concept Artist Alan Reynaud .

Considering the high quality of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , it would be a shame if Nintendo Switch 2 owners would never get to experience it. At the same time, it's understandable how Sandfall Interactive sees the port as a challenge, given the studio's small size. The current generation Nintendo system has already seen some impressive ports like Cyberpunk 2077 and the Final Fantasy VII Remake series, but they were handled by much bigger studios with developers and resources to invest.

Hopefully Lumen Lite , which has been created specifically for handhelds like the Nintendo Switch 2 , will help this port become a reality.

About the author : Francesco De Meo has been covering video games and technology since 2012, starting his career at small outlets like Gamersyndrome and GeekSnack. After joining Wccftech gaming section in 2015, he quickly expanded his video gaming coverage with in-depth reporting, interviews with iconic industry figures such as Grasshopper Manufacture founder and No More Heroes creator Goichi "Suda51" Suda, Resident Evil series creator Shinji Mikami, Team NINJA's president and Nioh series director Fumihiko Yasuda, and Silent Hill creator Keiichiro Toyama, reviews and on-the-ground coverage of major industry events such as Gamescom and E3. When he's not reporting or reviewing, Francesco can be found playing the genres he loves most, spending time with his six cats, reading, writing music, playing guitar and drumming for his progressive rock band.

items.summary: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 may still end up on Nintendo Switch 2 at some point on the future, but it would be a “big technical challenge”. The RPG originally released on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X and S. Sandfall Interactive co-founder Tom Guillermin said in a recent interview that a Nintendo Switch 2 version would be tough “because we...
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 may still end up on Nintendo Switch 2 at some point on the future, but it would be a “big technical challenge”.

The RPG originally released on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X and S. Sandfall Interactive co-founder Tom Guillermin said in a recent interview that a Nintendo Switch 2 version would be tough “because we tried to do something beautiful with the game, but of course, the Switch 2 is not as powerful as the PlayStation or the Xbox Series X.”

Creative director Guillaume Broche added that Unreal Engine 5 being a part of the equation doesn’t help things since “a lot of features” aren’t compatible with Nintendo’s console. That said, lead character and concept artist Alan Reynaud pointed out that the new Lumen Lite feature may provide to be beneficial.

I think your fans are quite curious about a Switch 2 version. Do you think Expedition 33 would be able to run on the Switch 2? And do you have any such plans at the moment?

Guillaume Broche: We are interested in looking for a way to do it, but it’s too early for us to announce anything at this point.

Tom Guillermin: It’s a big technical challenge because we tried to do something beautiful with the game, but of course, the Switch 2 is not as powerful as the PlayStation or the Xbox Series X. So, it’s an important thing for us to consider, especially given the size of our studio.

Do you think Unreal Engine 5 is also a challenge when trying to bring Expedition 33 to the Switch 2?

Guillaume Broche: Yes, a lot of features don’t work on Switch 2.

Alan Reynaud: They’re introducing features like Lumen Lite now, which is easier to run than the standard Lumen, but these things take time to roll out, so we’ll have to consider the updates coming from Unreal Engine to determine what to do.

Unreal Engine 5.8 just started to roll out about a month ago. With it came Lumen Light and Epic Games has indicated that it will be pretty impactful for Nintendo Switch 2. You can learn more about it here .

items.title: "It's a sad decision." Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 developers on the end of physical disc production and why they pushed for a physical release despite the drawbacks
items.summary: Interview with Sandfall Interactive's core members about what physical games mean to them.
items.content:
Home Interviews “It’s a sad decision.” Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 developers on the end of physical disc production and why they pushed for a physical release despite the drawbacks Interview with Sandfall Interactive's core members about what physical games mean to them.

Interviews 2026-07-29 00:01 Genki 3 Epic Games Japan and Sandfall Interactive recently hosted a Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 postmortem event in Yokohama, Japan, where the developers shared technical insights into the making of 2025’s Game of the Year. Following the event, AUTOMATON sat down with the team and took the opportunity to ask about their thoughts on physical game releases. With PlayStation set to end game disc production in 2028, the developers briefly reflected on why they insisted on releasing Expedition 33 physically despite the added challenges, and discussed why they believe physical editions remain important to video games as a medium.

Guillaume Broche – Sandfall Interactive CEO and Creative Director Tom Guillermin – Sandfall Interactive Co-founder and CTO Alan Reynaud – Lead Character and Concept Artist Alexandre Breton – Technical Artist

For more about Sandfall Interactive’s Japanese influences, thoughts on Unreal Engine, and studio upsizing, check out part one of this interview .

— PlayStation recently announced that it will end physical disk production in 2028. What are your thoughts on that?

Guillaume Broche: Personally, I find it super sad because I really like video game stores. And even if nowadays, I play mainly on PC myself, we have a lot of people on the team who play on PS5 and love to collect physical discs. I think it’s part of the beauty of art too – that it’s something tangible that you can touch. I completely appreciate that people want to have their rows of DVDs and games and just feel that they own them. So I think it’s a shame. I mean, business-wise, I can understand why it may make sense, but I think in terms of the artistry of video games, it’s a sad decision.

Tom Guillermin: In our discussions with our publisher prior to the release of Expedition 33, the question of whether or not to do a physical release cropped up. A physical release adds more constraints because you have to account for the production time of the physical items, and you also earn less money per copy.

But for us, physical was something special. We also felt that the game could be special to players, and that they would want to, as Guillaume said, hold it in their hands.

So even though it made things harder and meant less money per unit, it was important for us to provide players who want to have the physical game in their hands with an option. Because that’s what we value as players too.

Guillaume Broche: To add to that, there were two very strong moments when the game released. After launch, we went to a video game store to buy our own game (laughs). Just as a gesture. And another strong memory I have is when someone from Japan sent me a picture [of our game] from a video game store – in Akihabara I think – in Japanese writing and all. I felt like a kid when I saw it. I was like “Yeah, it’s real!” It starts feeling real when you see it in stores. Alan Reynaud: Even now when I’m going to the supermarket or something, if I see our game in a store, it always makes my day. It’s a bit selfish, because it’s our game, but it always makes me go “Oh!”

Knowing that may not be possible again makes me a bit sad. And maybe it’s the child in me, but I like to go outside, buy a game, and come back home with it. It’s a nice feeling.

Alexandre Breton: And it’s not just because it’s “our game.” I think what’s cool [about physical games in general] is that a few years later, you’ll have your box, and you can hold it and look at the title and remember all the memories that are linked to the game.

Alan Reynaud: I think the same principle can apply to manga. It’s nice to read on your phone and stuff, but having a real book is just a different feeling. And I don’t think we could imagine a world where manga is just scanned and stored on your computer. It would be sad to not have it in your library. I think the same applies for games. Sure, it makes more sense business-wise, but you lose the spirit of it.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is available for PC ( Steam ), PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 director says eliminating limitations in development is a "big mistake." We talk to Sandfall Interactive about staying small, Japanese influences, and what's next
items.summary: Interview with Sandfall Interactive at the Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 postmortem in Yokohama, Japan.
items.content:
Home Interviews Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 director says eliminating limitations in development is a “big mistake.” We talk to Sandfall Interactive about staying small, Japanese influences, and what’s next Interview with Sandfall Interactive at the Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 postmortem in Yokohama, Japan.

Game Development , Interviews 2026-07-29 00:00 Genki 3 Epic Games Japan and Sandfall Interactive recently hosted a Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 postmortem event in Yokohama, Japan, offering a behind-the-scenes look at the development of 2025’s Game of the Year. After the presentation, AUTOMATON sat down with the developers to discuss their Japanese influences, their views on JRPGs, why Unreal Engine was the right choice for their small team, and why the studio has no intention of significantly increasing its headcount.

Participants are as follows: Guillaume Broche – Sandfall Interactive CEO and Creative Director Tom Guillermin – Sandfall Interactive Co-founder and CTO Alan Reynaud – Lead Character and Concept Artist Alexandre Breton – Technical Artist

For more about Sandfall Interactive’s views on physical disc production ending , check out part two of this interview.

—Could you tell me about the influence Japanese games and anime have had on your approach to game design? What were some of the biggest Japanese influences on Expedition 33?

Guillaume Broche: Growing up, I’d say 95% of the games I was playing were Japanese games, so I’ve always been super influenced by them. My first real video game memory was Final Fantasy VIII on PS1. Before that, I’d also played some games on the Mega Drive, but they were smaller titles and I don’t remember them very well because I was too young. But to this day, JRPGs in particular continue to be one of my favorite genres.

And of course, one of the main influences in my life is the Final Fantasy series and the work of Hironobu Sakaguchi, including titles like Lost Odyssey and Blue Dragon. Other JRPGs that have influenced me include the Shin Megami Tensei and Persona series, the Atelier series, and Tales of Vesperia. I’ve said it a million times by now, but I pretty much play almost all JRPGs available at the time. Not every single one, but really a lot.

Obviously, Expedition 33’s gameplay is very much inspired by the older Final Fantasy games. It’s turn-based, and you have three characters facing three monsters, so they were definitely a massive inspiration.

Also, as I grew up, I think I’d been missing that kind of game ever since Lost Odyssey. Lost Odyssey was, for me, the last big realistic turn-based game. You still have titles like Yakuza and Persona coming out now, but they’re more stylized. On the other hand, I felt like the grand, epic, realistic kind of turn-based games like Final Fantasy X and Last Odyssey didn’t exist anymore. Since that’s my favorite type of game personally, I just wanted to make it.

—How about anime? I believe you’ve mentioned being a big Ghibli fan, but have you drawn influence from any specific titles?

Guillaume Broche: Yes, I know that for a lot of people in the West, Disney is a big part of their childhood memories, but for me, it’s Ghibli. Especially Spirited Away. I think I’ve seen that movie 50 times, no joke. It’s a masterpiece from A to Z, and I also love other films by the studio.

Also, I think one of the anime that inspired me for Expedition 33’s story was Attack on Titan. I really like the idea of a group of heroes fighting together, and I especially love the uniform. When you see any character from Attack on Titan, you instantly know they’re an Attack on Titan character because of the uniform. That’s something I really wanted to bring over into Expedition 33, making the game recognizable just from its uniforms.

In fact, I’m rewatching Attack on Titan right now because I haven’t watched it for at least six years. I’m on season four now, almost at the end, and really, it’s an absolute masterpiece for me.

Alan Reynaud: For the characters, there were a lot of anime that had a big influence on us. One of them is Bleach. I have to mention Bleach because the character designs in the series are spectacular. One of the things we took from it was designs that are super simple yet incredibly memorable. We wanted to have something like that, with a “rule of cool” approach. I’d say that was a big inspiration for the character creation.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available in Arabic!
items.summary: Expeditioners! Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text! This brings the total number of supported langua
items.content:
Expeditioners!

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text!

This brings the total number of supported languages to 20!

With the new Arabic language support, we had to consider additional changes to the game’s UI to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience for Arabic-speaking players around the world.

Adding Arabic localization has been a true team effort over many months, from the incredible adaptation and localization work carried out by the linguists, to reworking the vast majority of the user interface for right-to-left reading, all the way through localization testing.

Every team involved brought passion and dedication to making this possible, and we couldn’t be more grateful for their work. We hope this update makes the story feel even more personal to our players.

Today’s update also includes some additional fixes and improvements. Read the full patch notes here!

Thank you all so much for your continued support! <3

Tomorrow comes.

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.title: 1st Anniversary of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
items.summary: Expeditioners!! Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special
items.content:
Expeditioners!! 

 

Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. 

 

To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special piece of artwork that we hope you will enjoy! 

8 Million Copies Sold

We're so thrilled, and honestly still quite overwhelmed, to announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has officially reached 8 million copies sold!

Thank you so so much to every single person who has played, created art, shared, streamed, discussed, and supported this game!!

Game Update: New Haircuts + Patch Notes

We've pushed a fun little update live today: new haircuts are now available in-game, giving the expedition even more style to strut around in! 💅 

For the full list of changes, fixes, and improvements, you can read the patch notes here

Community Emotes

Our community is packed with phenomenally talented artists and we wanted to celebrate that today.  

We commissioned some of our amazing community creators to design official Expedition 33 emotes for you to use in your own channels! 

A massive thank you to IrunoArt, comickergirl (Sarah Leuver), and Bugyakis for their brilliant work on each of these!!

They're FREE to download and use here

Official Baguette Merch

In the mood to add some baguette to your wardrobe? 

We’ve partnered with Orcival and Le Béret Français to bring you the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 striped shirt and beret for your cosplays! 🥖    You can purchase the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Orcival mariniere here

And the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Le Béret Français beret is available to buy here

On top of that, keep an eye out for a limited number of units of the Monolith Set to be back in stock from our partners at Laced and Pix n' Love soon!! 

And Finally… Cake

It's been a big day for us. Thank you for making it possible. 🎂 

And if you know someone who wants to pick up the game, we're running a 20% sale right now on Steam - As well as some fun merchandise goodies available on our merch page!

Merch Page

From the bottom of our hearts, we’re so thankful to each and every one of you – this has been the best year of our lives, thanks to you. 

 

- The Expedition 33 Team

items.content:
Expeditioners!

Thank you for all of your reports - the details for the fixes in this patch are written out below:

Update On Sirene Crash

  • After a thorough internal investigation, the crash that occurred after defeating Sirene can no longer be reproduced on our end. If you keep getting this issue, we’d suggest updating your Windows to the latest version. If the issue persists, please submit a report and we’ll continue investigating.

    [/*]

Bug Fixes & Improvements

Photo Mode

  • Fixed facial hair of characters being blurred in the Photo Mode on the close distance if Shading was set to Epic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue in Photo mode that prevented the Inner Cone Angle and Outer Cone Angle options from affecting the shape of the preview light source.

    [/*]

  • Photo Mode's spotlight and point light display has been modified to improve their visibility

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where loading a save while picking up a journal could cause that journal to disappear permanently and become impossible to collect again.

    • Missing journals are now also restored retroactively when loading affected saves.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Fixed a soft lock that could occur, during the Chromatic Glissando encounter in Sirene’s Dress level, when a dead expeditioner equipped with Shortcut and Second Chance pictos was swallowed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on Gestral Beach where using the Rematch option after losing the volleyball minigame could create a blocked save.

    [/*]

  • Fixed a visual issue where characters affected by Inverted would not have the correct colour effect applied to their eyes.

    [/*]

Environment

  • Fixed various environment issues (collisions, misplaced assets, missing or incorrect footsteps SFX) across Verso's Drafts, the World Map, and other levels.

    [/*]

  • Fixed various lighting issues on Steam Deck in Verso’s Drafts, Endless Tower and Stone Wave Cliffs levels.

    [/*]

As always, thanks for your support and for your reports via the official Typeform - We'll continue monitoring the reports coming in and working on future fixes!

~ The Expedition 33 Team
